quiz.title: CAT Quant Pattern Quiz
quiz.intro: Eight CAT-level questions spread across arithmetic, algebra, number systems, geometry and modern maths — the same mix the quant section tests. Answer each, then press Check my score.

questions.explanation: 720 = 2⁴ × 3² × 5. Add one to each power and multiply: (4+1)(2+1)(1+1) = 5 × 3 × 2 = 30.

questions.q: In an arithmetic progression the 7th term is 34 and the 13th term is 64. What is the common difference?
questions.explanation: Six steps separate the 7th and 13th terms, and the value rises by 64 − 34 = 30. So d = 30 ÷ 6 = 5.

questions.q: In what ratio should rice costing Rs 30/kg be mixed with rice costing Rs 40/kg to make a mixture worth Rs 36/kg?
What is the distance between the points (2, 3) and (5, 7)?
How many ways can a committee of 3 be formed from 7 people?
questions.explanation: Order does not matter, so use combinations: C(7,3) = (7 × 6 × 5) ÷ (3 × 2 × 1) = 35.

questions.q: If log₂ x = 5, what is x?
A cylinder has radius 7 cm and height 10 cm. What is its volume? (Take π = 22/7.)
A fair die is rolled twice. What is the probability that the two numbers add up to 8?
questions.explanation: The pairs summing to 8 are (2,6), (3,5), (4,4), (5,3) and (6,2) — 5 outcomes out of 36, so the probability is 5/36.

faq.q: What is the pattern of the CAT quantitative aptitude section?
faq.a: The quant section carries 22 questions to be solved in 40 minutes, mixing MCQs and TITA (type-in-the-answer) questions. There is no fixed split by topic, but arithmetic, algebra and geometry together usually dominate the paper.

faq.q: Which topics carry the most weight in CAT quant?
faq.a: Arithmetic — percentages, ratios, time-speed-distance, profit and loss — is the single largest bucket most years, followed closely by algebra and number systems. Geometry, mensuration and modern maths round out the rest.

faq.q: How much time should I spend per question?
faq.a: Roughly 1.5 to 2 minutes on average, but strong scorers do not solve every question. Clear the easy and medium ones first, mark the hard ones, and come back only if time allows — accuracy matters more than attempt count.

faq.q: Is there negative marking in CAT quant?
faq.a: Yes for MCQs: +3 for a correct answer and −1 for a wrong one. TITA questions carry no penalty, so it is always worth entering your best answer on those.
